title: Are Phone Cleaner Apps Safe? What to Check
meta_description: Are phone cleaner apps safe? Learn the warning signs, the permissions a cleaner really needs and how CleanKoach handles your files, ads and data on your phone.
tagline: Warning signs, permissions and what to verify
quick_answer: Some phone cleaner apps are safe and some are not, so check before you install. A safe cleaner asks only for the permissions it needs, works without an account, analyses files on your phone and does not scare you into tapping. CleanKoach analyses files on your device, never uploads them and has no accounts.
intro: Cleaner apps have a mixed reputation because a few behave badly. Here is what to look for, what CleanKoach asks for and why, and how you can check any app yourself.

sections.h2: What can go wrong with a cleaner
sections.html:
• Fake alerts: warnings that your phone is infected or overheating, used to push you to tap.
  • Too many permissions: access to contacts, messages or location that a cleaner does not need.
  • Files sent away: photos or scan results uploaded to a server.
  • Hidden costs: a free scan that ends in a surprise subscription.
  • Aggressive ads: pop-ups outside the app.

sections.h2: Ads and your data, stated plainly
sections.html: CleanKoach shows ads through Google AdMob. When ads are served, Google may collect your advertising ID and standard ad-interaction data under Google's own privacy policy. That is separate from your files, which stay on your phone. In the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom you are asked for consent first. If you buy Pro, the ads are removed and the app no longer collects an advertising ID.

sections.h2: How to check any app yourself
sections.html:
1. Read the permissions before installing and again in Android Settings under Apps.
  2. Read the privacy policy and look for what is collected.
  3. Keep Google Play Protect on. It checks apps for harmful behaviour.
  4. Deny what is not needed. A good cleaner still works without optional permissions.
  5. Uninstall anything that pops up outside the app or frightens you.

faqs.a: Some are and some are not. Check the permissions, whether it needs an account, where files are analysed and how it handles alerts and ads.
CleanKoach analyses your files on your phone, never uploads them, has no accounts and deletes nothing until you choose it and Android confirms.

faqs.q: What permissions does a cleaner really need?
faqs.a: Access to photos, videos and audio is enough for the main tools. Anything else should be optional and explained.

faqs.q: Does CleanKoach read my messages or contacts?
faqs.a: No. It does not ask for access to contacts, messages or location.

faqs.q: Why does CleanKoach need Usage Access?
faqs.a: Only for Activity Monitor, which shows app usage over the last 24 hours. It is optional and the data stays on your device.

faqs.q: Does CleanKoach collect any data through ads?
faqs.a: When ads are served, Google may collect your advertising ID and ad-interaction data as described in Google's privacy policy. Pro removes the ads and the app then no longer collects an advertising ID.

faqs.q: Can a cleaner app harm my phone?
faqs.a: A badly made or malicious one can, by deleting files you wanted or by pushing unwanted apps. Check permissions and reviews first, and keep Play Protect on.

faqs.q: How do I check an app I already installed?
faqs.a: Open Android Settings, then Apps, choose the app and review its permissions. Run a Play Protect scan from the Play Store.

faqs.q: Will CleanKoach show fake virus warnings?
faqs.a: No. CleanKoach does not show fake virus alerts. Its only notifications are optional weekly cleanup reminders and storage alerts that you turn on yourself.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay for CleanKoach to be safe?
faqs.a: No. Every feature is free. Pro only removes ads.
